gen-gf-hi-melody-fs-recia: Hi Melody is all hand-drawn tiles, pressed tightly together. Recia's moderate contrast, neither stark nor flat, keeps a few lines of text reading sharp and authoritative without any fuss.
gen-gf-hi-melody-sora: Hi Melody looks hand-drawn, with letters huddled like pressed tiles. Sora takes over underneath, geometric and precise, its curves turning corners without any pressure swell, built for brief bursts of reading.
gen-gf-hi-melody-space-grotesk: Hi Melody feels hand-drawn and inviting, its letters huddled close like pressed-together tiles. And Space Grotesk draws each glyph as a ribbon of constant width, comfortable for a bit of reading.
gen-gf-iansui-fs-neco: Friendly and hand-drawn, Iansui keeps its diagonals as thick as its upright strokes. Neco swells gently from hairline to stem, dignified enough to carry a short run of text without its letters pinching shut.
gen-gf-iansui-fs-recia: Personal and hand-drawn, Iansui writes its lowercase a without any thin hairline strokes. Recia is the serif underneath, faintly modulated yet steady, with generous openings that keep brief reading easy going.
gen-gf-iansui-fs-spline-sans: Spline Sans keeps its vertical and horizontal strokes at identical weight, with wide gaps between curve ends and stems. Iansui handles brief friendly moments; Spline Sans does the steadier lifting.
gen-gf-iansui-outfit: Iansui writes friendly, hand-drawn letters with gently flared curve ends. Outfit, a sans-serif, finishes its curves well before they close and never swells or thins, so it backs the heading quietly when text stays brief.
gen-gf-itim-fs-asap: Itim's casual handwriting climbs only a short way from midline to ascender. Asap does the steady work, its open c arcs and near-capital body height keeping text readable once the heading's done.
gen-gf-itim-manrope: Itim is casual handwriting, happiest in a line or two. Manrope is the brighter half, with open curve mouths, a minimal cap-to-lowercase step and a pen line holding one width throughout.
gen-gf-jaini-fs-paquito: Jaini crowds its letters like logs in a river boom. Paquito settles in below, confident and approachable, its lowercase barely shorter than its capitals, good for a few lines at most.
